reason: User clause: an office for software and ITES, and no other use without consent. Restricts use of these premises only.
The Restricted Period (cl. 1C) is 2 years after the deed ends, within 5 km. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
While the lease lasts, the Lessors will not let other units in the complex to a competitor. A restriction on how the Lessors deal with their own property, in-term only.

Courts at Mumbai 'only', said to be where the Lessor's registered office is, but the preamble puts that office in Karol Bagh, New Delhi. The premises are in Noida and the Lessee is in Delhi. If the Lessor in fact has its office in Mumbai, those courts can hear claims against it (s.20 CPC) but not claims about the property. Clause 31 names the Delhi courts and clause 30 sends disputes to arbitration. Whether a competent court is left depends on facts outside the text. Refer.

The Lessor may appropriate the deposit towards sums due 'in its opinion' and refund the balance. A right of appropriation: the opinion is not made final and no forum is excluded, so the Lessee can still claim any wrongful deduction. Not a s.28 ouster.
Civil courts at Bangalore and no others; the premises are in Bangalore. Courts with jurisdiction anyway; cl. 16 arbitration stands.

Goodwill of the travel desk is sold and the restraint lasts while the buyer carries on the business, but it applies 'anywhere whatsoever'. No specified local limits, so Exception 1 does not apply. Void.
A claim not notified within 45 days 'shall stand extinguished'. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period, against the 3-year period (s.43 of the 1996 Act). Void.

The Lessor sold the goodwill of its warehousing business to the Lessee and restrains itself within the taluk (a specified local limit) for as long as the buyer carries on a like business at the Property. All three conditions of Exception 1 are met; reasonableness is for the court. Refer (as PO-50).
A written agreement to refer differences that 'have arisen' over the deposit under the previous lease to arbitration by a retired judge. Saved by Exception 2.
A step under the contract (drawings 15 days before fit-out; Lessor to respond in 10 days). Nothing about claims or courts.
Repairs within 14 days of the Lessor's notice. A step under the contract.

The renewal option is unobjectionable. But if the Lessee does not renew, it may not carry on its business within 2 km for 18 months after the Term. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold, and void to that extent.
Business at the premises outside the Operating Hours (cl. 1E) needs the Lessor's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. A restriction on use of these premises only.

In-term only, but it restrains the Lessee from opening another outlet within 3 km, which is business elsewhere, not the use of these premises. The rent includes a turnover share, which is the commercial justification a court would weigh (a radius clause protecting the landlord's income). That turns on context outside the text. Refer.
Arbitration must start within 30 days of the dispute, and 'after that, the claim is gone'. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Void.
No action against the Lessor unless commenced within 90 days of the breach, against 3 years under Art. 55. Shortens the time to sue. Void.
Disconnection of electricity and water after 30 days' default and 7 days' notice. A self-help remedy, not a limit on going to court (as PO-44).
Holding over at three times the daily rent. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.
Three years from the breach, the same as Art. 55. Not shorter, so not void.
A cap on the Lessor's total liability at three months' rent. Limits recovery, not access to court.

For 24 months after the deed ends, no font or software facility, and no office space for one, within 5 km, binding the Lessee and companies it controls. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
The Lessor's certificate binds for payment only, 'without prejudice' to the Lessee's right to arbitrate the computation under cl. 18(d). The forum is preserved (as PO-42).
The Lessor is 'released' from latent-defect claims unless notified within 6 months after the Handover Date (cl. I(f)). Discharge from liability on the expiry of a period. Void.
Any question, difference or dispute 'shall be referred to arbitration' under the 1996 Act, with a final award. A binding arbitration agreement, saved by Exception 1.

The Lessor's own certificate of arrears is final and cannot be disputed 'in any proceeding, judicial, arbitral or otherwise'. One party decides and every forum is shut out, overriding the arbitration clause in Article XXVIII. Void to that extent.

The guarantee is to carry a claim period of 12 months after its expiry, after which the bank is discharged. That discharge term is stipulated in a bank guarantee, with a period of not less than one year from the specified event, so it is saved by Exception 3. The lease only requires such a guarantee and does not itself cut down the parties' rights.

The right to require rectification 'shall lapse absolutely' on the Snag List Date (30 days after possession, cl. 1E), and the Lessor then has no liability. The right is extinguished and the party discharged on the expiry of a period. Void.
No suit, arbitration or other proceeding for loss from interruption of power or water, and the claims are waived. An absolute bar for that class of claims (as PO-08, PO-38). Void to that extent.
No injunction against sale or mortgage of the Building; the Lessee's claim sounds only in damages. The court remains open for damages, so this is a remedies question, not s.28 (as PO-29).

The Escalation Procedure (cl. 1B) is talks, then arbitration only 'if both parties then so agree', which is not an arbitration agreement. The clause makes that the 'only' route and bars 'any court or other forum', which includes the cl. 10A tribunal. On its terms an absolute bar, void. (Clause 10A survives it.)
During the term, the Lessors will not let any other part of the Building to a medical transcription business. A restriction on how the Lessors deal with their own property, in-term only.

No suit, arbitration or other proceeding about the Excluded Matters (cl. 1B: service interruptions, terrace access, parking). An absolute bar for those classes of claims, overriding cl. 18. Void to that extent.
'All disputes ... shall be settled by arbitration' by three arbitrators under the 1996 Act, with a final award. A binding arbitration agreement, saved by Exception 1.

A jointly appointed consultant fixes the renewal rent 'as an expert and not as an arbitrator', and his figure is binding. An agreed way of fixing a term, not an ouster; courts are not expressly excluded. Refer, per the BP-7 approach, though I would lean valid: this fills in the bargain rather than deciding a dispute about rights.
Query within 10 days so the Lessor can verify, and the clause says expressly that nothing follows from a late query. No right lost.
Report electrical defects within the Defect Notice Period (15 days, cl. 1A) so repairs can be made. No consequence attached; no right lost.

Not the BP-7 'refer' case: the architect is the Lessor's own, and the clause expressly says no suit, arbitration or other proceeding lies before any court or tribunal. A party's nominee plus express exclusion of every forum (as PO-49). Void.
The Restraint Period (cl. 1B) is 4 years from when the Lessee ceases to occupy, so this is post-lease (Noida). No goodwill sold. Void.
A Cure Period (30 days after notice, cl. 1C) before termination, without prejudice to other remedies. A step under the contract; no right is lost.
From the Separation Date (cl. 1C) for 3 years, within 10 km, unless the Lessor consents. A post-lease restraint; the consent proviso does not save it, and no goodwill is sold. Void.

The Lessor will not let a competitor's name be shown on the Building during the lease and for 18 months after. During the term it is valid (the Lessor's own property); the post-term period is the doubtful part (as PO-43). Refer.

The Lessee's own certificate of the completion date binds SIPCOT, which may not question it 'in any court, arbitration or other proceeding'. One party decides and every forum is shut out; s.28 protects the Lessor as well. Void.
The Transition Period (cl. 1D) is the 30 days after expiry, and the restraint runs 24 months beyond that, within 5 km. Entirely post-lease, with no goodwill sold. Void.
The electricity bill is 'deemed to have been accepted ... as correct and binding' unless disputed within 15 days. Deemed acceptance on the expiry of a period (as PO-24, PO-66). Void.
